mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, reducing the cost of capital and increasing the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 0.2 percentage points over three months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate signals a coordinated monetary easing and labor market improvement, which reduces recession risk and boosts corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by robust consumer spending, rising housing starts (HOUST) signal strong demand for durable goods and construction, which typically precedes higher corporate revenues and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST rises, or the Rank IC for HOUST in late-cycle is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing and industrial output, which supports economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts above 0.5% signals strong consumer confidence and demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector's positive spillovers boost the broader economy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a recessionary regime, a high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals deepening economic distress, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings face immediate pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during recession when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE in recession is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising retail sales figure (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, which is a key driver of corporate revenue growth and typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS rises, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
